confirmedFlows.complexityRationale: Unidirectional scheduled-sync. Standard pattern: QB query with LastModifiedDate watermark (April 1 fiscal year offset required), upsert to Salesforce Agreement via QB_InvoiceId__c external ID. Well-understood pattern with no novel transformations.

potentialFlows.rationale: Maria is adding new titles to QB and Salesforce separately. Without sync, the QB Item list and SF Product catalog will diverge — breaking UC1 line item matching and UC4 cost lookup. Deferred in May 8 call pending Maria's input on system of record (QB or SF). This is a dependency risk for UC1 and UC4, not merely a nice-to-have. Promote to confirmed if Maria confirms one system of record and the divergence risk is real.

Holly: sales ships materials before a closed-won agreement on a CCR. When the Agreement arrives in Salesforce, UC1 would fire and create a QB invoice — but if materials were already shipped and invoiced via CCR, this creates a duplicate. The CCR fulfillment state must stamp the incoming Agreement before UC1 fires. Promote to confirmed once CCR workflow in Salesforce is mapped and the flag field identified.

Each order decrements inventory in QB. UC4 (scheduled sync) covers inventory quantities but with a polling lag. Between sync runs, Salesforce Inventory__c shows stale available-stock figures. A real-time or near-real-time decrement event from QB would keep Holly's dashboard accurate between scheduled runs. Partially covered by UC4 — promote to confirmed only if clients identify the lag as a business problem post-UC4 go-live.

p0Blockers.title: QuickBooks Version Confirmation
p0Blockers.clientAction:
Please confirm which QuickBooks product your team uses — we need this before any integration work can begin:
  (a) QuickBooks Online — the web-based version you access at app.qbo.intuit.com in a browser.
  (b) QuickBooks Desktop Pro or Premier — installed as a program on a Windows PC.
  (c) QuickBooks Enterprise — the advanced desktop version.

If you're not sure: the easiest check is whether you open QuickBooks in a web browser (Online) or by clicking an icon on your desktop (Desktop/Enterprise). Maria Gonzalez-Pettway or Crystal Robinson should know which version is in use.
p0Blockers.body: QBO path: mule-quickbooks-online-connector 3.0.0 (REST/OAuth 2.0) — clean cloud-to-cloud integration. QB Desktop/Enterprise path: NO native MuleSoft connector; NO REST API. Requires QBXML Web Connector on the Windows machine running QB, then a bridge layer (CData JDBC or Conductor REST relay) to reach CloudHub 2.0 — adds $1,500–$5,000/yr licensing cost and on-prem relay maintenance. DataSkate recommendation if Desktop: assess upgrade to QB Online first. FK-020 verified: never assume QBO.
bundledWith: QB Connected App setup at developer.intuit.com
QB sandbox company provisioning for integration testing
QB OAuth credentials authorization (Crystal or Maria to authorize)
Confirm QB fiscal year April 1 is correctly set in company settings

p0Blockers.title: Inventory Spreadsheet Storage Location
p0Blockers.clientAction:
We need to know where Holly Wale's inventory demand worksheet is stored before we can build the integration. Please confirm one of the following:
  (a) Holly's local laptop — this CANNOT work with our integration platform (cloud-hosted; no access to local files). The file would need to be moved to a shared cloud location before we can begin.
  (b) SharePoint or OneDrive — we can connect to this; please provide the SharePoint site URL and file path.
  (c) Google Drive or Google Sheets — we can connect to this; Chloe (IT) will need to provide a Google Service Account credential so our system can read the file.

Holly Wale (hwale@agilemind.com) or Chloe (IT Director) can confirm this.
p0Blockers.body: CloudHub 2.0 has an ephemeral local filesystem — the File connector cannot read local PC paths. If client insists on local-only and will not migrate: SFTP drop-zone on a cloud server is the only bridge (adds operational overhead and manual step for Holly). If QB version confirms QB Online and inventory lives fully in QB, UC3 may be replaced by UC4 entirely (QB as sole inventory source) — making this P0 conditional on the UC3 design decision.
bundledWith: Google Service Account provisioning (Chloe/IT) if Google Sheets path
Azure AD app registration and Graph API permissions (Chloe/IT) if OneDrive/SharePoint path
Holly column-header documentation for DataWeave mapping — headers must be stable before DWL is written

p0Blockers.title: Salesforce State/Country Picklist Format
p0Blockers.clientAction: Please confirm whether Salesforce State/Country Picklists are enabled in your org, and share a sample record showing the mailing state field value from an Opportunity or Agreement (e.g., 'California' vs 'CA' or 'US-CA'). This determines the key format used in the ISBN lookup table DataSkate will configure.
p0Blockers.body: If State/Country Picklists are enabled, mailing state values on Opportunity/Agreement are ISO 3166 subdivision codes (e.g., US-CA, not California). The configurable ISBN lookup table (State × Product → ISBN) must use whichever format Salesforce stores. Writing the DataWeave mapping before this is confirmed risks a silent key mismatch that produces no ISBN match and routes all invoices to manual review.
bundledWith: ISBN lookup table data collection — AgileMind to provide the current state→ISBN mapping used today (even if informal/in someone's head)

pricing.recommendedModelRationale: AgileMind has no dedicated MuleSoft operations team — Chloe is IT Director but no integration engineer or MuleSoft developer is on staff. The $0 upfront IaaS model removes the budget barrier given their stated cash-flow sensitivity and '$0–$2,500' implementation partner cost expectation; the $2,500 kickoff retainer fits precisely within that range and is fully credited at go-live. Ongoing managed service covers the QB OAuth refresh token rotation risk (100-day expiry = a silent production break without automated rotation) and connector upgrades — both are operational concerns AgileMind cannot manage internally. At 4 flows, the implementation-only fee ($14,000) is relatively modest, making IaaS less financially dominant than at 10 flows, but the operational support argument is the primary driver at their team size and technical capacity.
